title: U.S. House · Arizona's 1st District
area: Northeast Phoenix metro area, including Scottsdale, Paradise Valley, Cave Creek, Fountain Hills, and part of north Mesa.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Republican David Schweikert, who had held the seat since 2011, did not seek re-election and instead ran for governor of Arizona. Amish Shah won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.5% of the vote over Marlene Galán-Woods, Jonathan Treble, and Rick McCartney. Jay Feely won the Republican primary with 49.8% over Joseph Chaplik and John Trobough. Monica Alponte won the Libertarian primary. Two write-in candidates, Gage Thunder (no party preference) and Dev Gupta (independent), are also on the general-election ballot. Cook Political Report rated the district R+1; in 2024 Schweikert defeated Shah 51.9%-48.1% while Donald Trump carried the district 51.1%-48.0%.

candidates.name: Amish Shah
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.5% of the vote

summary.text: Amish Shah is an emergency-medicine physician and the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He served in the Arizona House of Representatives from 2019 to 2024 and was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to Rep. David Schweikert. His campaign website says he has focused on teacher pay, small businesses, and public health and safety.

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, to parents who immigrated from India in the 1960s, according to Wikipedia. Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Northwestern University in 1997, an M.D. from Northwestern University in 2001, and a master's in public health from the University of California, Berkeley in 2003.

Completed a residency in emergency medicine in New York City and joined the faculty of Mount Sinai Medical Center, where he worked on a project to improve player safety in the NFL. He was a team physician for the New York Jets for five seasons, then moved to Arizona for a sports medicine fellowship at the University of Arizona.

Worked as an attending physician with Mayo Clinic, Dignity Health, and IASIS Healthcare, and as chief medical officer of Urgent Consult; as of 2023 he was an emergency physician at Mayo Clinic Arizona.

Entered politics in 2018, winning one of two seats in Arizona's 24th legislative district after defeating incumbent Rep. Ken Clark and others in the Democratic primary. He was sworn into the Arizona House on January 14, 2019.

Served in the Arizona House of Representatives, District 24 (2019-2023) and, after redistricting, District 5 (2023-2024), re-elected in 2020 and 2022. His sponsored bills focused largely on health care, including prior-authorization forms, emergency medical transport, and physician peer support.
Won a six-candidate Democratic primary for Arizona's 1st Congressional District in 2024 with 23.5% of the vote, then lost the general election to incumbent Rep. David Schweikert 51.9%-48.1%.
Announced a second run for the seat in May 2025 and won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 39.4% of the vote, ahead of Marlene Galan-Woods (34.4%), Jonathan Treble, and Rick McCartney.
According to his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia, he has had a record of working across party lines, and had "more bills signed into law than any Arizona Democrat in the last decade."

priorities.text: Says he has 'a track record of being an independent voice working across party lines to put Arizona families first while standing up to extremist attacks on abortion and voting rights.'
priorities.quote: focused on increasing teacher pay, supporting small businesses, and improving public health and safety. He had more bills signed into law than any Arizona Democrat in the last decade. ... [He] has a track record of being an independent voice working across party lines to put Arizona families first while standing up to extremist attacks on abortion and voting rights.

priorities.text: Campaign material highlights increasing teacher pay and supporting small businesses as priorities from his state legislative record.

positions.summary: Voted no on SB 1164 (banning abortion after 15 weeks of pregnancy), which passed the Arizona House 31-26 on 2022-03-24.
Voted no on HB 2853 (expanding Arizona's Empowerment Scholarship Account voucher program to all students statewide), which passed the Arizona House 31-26 on 2022-06-22.

record.text: As an Arizona state representative, served on the House Appropriations Committee and House Health and Human Services Committee (2023-2024 session); the Transportation and Infrastructure and Health and Human Services Committees (2021-2022 session); and the Health and Human Services and Regulatory Affairs Committees (2019-2020 session).
Voted no on SB 1164 (banning abortion after 15 weeks of pregnancy), which passed the Arizona House 31-26 on 2022-03-24.
Voted no on HB 2853 (expanding Arizona's Empowerment Scholarship Account voucher program to all students statewide), which passed the Arizona House 31-26 on 2022-06-22.
Voted no on SB 1485 (removing voters from the Permanent Early Voting List if they do not vote by mail in two consecutive election cycles), which passed the Arizona House 31-29 on 2021-04-20.

candidates.name: Jay Feely
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 49.8% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Former NFL kicker and CBS sports analyst

summary.text: Jay Feely is a former NFL placekicker (2001-2014) and CBS football analyst, and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District, an open seat. He played college football at the University of Michigan and began his congressional campaign in 2025, first in the 5th District and later in the 1st. As of July 1, 2026, he had raised $2.53 million to Amish Shah's $1.83 million.

background.text: Born May 23, 1976, and attended Jesuit High School in Tampa, Florida, according to Wikipedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree in finance from the University of Michigan in 1998, where he was a four-year letterman as a kicker.
Began his professional career with the Florida Bobcats (1999) and Tampa Bay Storm (2000) of the Arena Football League.

Played as a kicker for six NFL teams from 2001 to 2014, including the Atlanta Falcons, New York Giants, Miami Dolphins, New York Jets, Arizona Cardinals (2010-2013), and Chicago Bears. He was named to the Pro Football Weekly All-Rookie team in 2001.
After retiring, joined CBS in 2015 as a college football analyst for CBS Sports Network and later worked as an NFL analyst and color commentator for CBS.
Announced in April 2025 that he would run as a Republican in Arizona's 5th District, then announced on December 19, 2025 that he would run in the 1st District instead.
Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 49.8% of the vote over Joseph Chaplik (35.7%) and John Trobough (14.5%); Wikipedia reports he was endorsed by President Donald Trump.
Lives in Gilbert, Arizona, with his wife, Rebecca; the couple have four children, according to Wikipedia. His campaign website cites his charitable work in the community.

priorities.text: Describes his approach as bringing the same 'unwavering commitment to having a positive impact' from his football and broadcasting career to public service, without detailing specific legislative proposals on his campaign site as of this research.
priorities.quote: never backed down from hard work or hesitated to stand up for what he knows is right. From the pressure-filled moments on the football field to the bright lights of the broadcast booth, and his deep involvement in the community through his charitable work, Jay has approached every chapter of his life with the same unwavering commitment to having a positive impact.

candidates.name: Monica Alponte

summary.text: Monica Alponte is the Libertarian nominee for Arizona's 1st Congressional District. She describes herself as a retired business writer, community leader, and former co-host of a conservative TV talk show, and is running on non-interventionist foreign policy, abolishing the IRS and Federal Reserve, and opposing government overreach into individual and property rights.

background.text: Describes herself as a retired business writer, an active community leader, and former co-host of a conservative TV talk show.
Says she began to part ways with the major parties in 2008 and has spent the past 21 years working with her Arizona county on road and driver safety and on homeowners' association (HOA) reform.
Is the Libertarian nominee on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for Arizona's 1st District.

priorities.text: Opposes U.S. involvement in foreign wars and says she will not accept money from foreign lobbies, including AIPAC, pledging to vote solely in American interests.
priorities.quote: Foreign wars are vehicles for waste, corruption, and money-laundering scams. I am committed to a policy of non-intervention and peace. I will not take money from foreign lobbies like AIPAC; I will show up and vote solely in the interests of Americans.

priorities.text: Wants to abolish the IRS and end the Federal Reserve's control of currency, favoring free markets without government interference.
priorities.quote: I stand for a simple, bold solution: Abolish the IRS, end the Federal Reserve’s monopoly on our currency, and return that wealth to the people.

priorities.text: Says government, from homeowners' associations to Congress, should serve rather than rule, and describes herself as a defender of free speech and the right to self-defense.
priorities.quote: From overreaching HOAs to the halls of Congress, the government should serve, not rule. I am a steadfast defender of your fundamental rights, including a pro-2A commitment to self-defense and an unwavering defense of free speech.

positions.summary: Describes herself as having a pro-Second Amendment commitment to the right of self-defense, opposing stricter gun laws.

candidates.researchNotes: Monica Alponte's Ballotpedia page had no separate Biography section, but she completed the 2026 Candidate Connection survey (checked https://ballotpedia.org/Monica_Alponte on 2026-09-25), which supplies her background, priorities, and one documented position here. Her survey answers do not directly address most of the guide's other 15 fixed issue statements (e.g., no specific statement on continuing U.S. military aid to Israel beyond declining AIPAC contributions, and no specific statement on taxing high earners versus her general call to abolish the IRS), so those were not added as `positions`.

researchNotes: This is an open, battleground seat. Candidate campaign websites for Shah and Feely did not render usable text content in this environment (JavaScript-rendered pages), so positions were drawn from quoted material on Ballotpedia's 2026 battleground-election summary rather than direct campaign-site issue pages; specific issue-by-issue positions could not be independently confirmed and are left out per the research standard rather than inferred. Monica Alponte (Libertarian nominee) completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, but her responses were not fetched within this research session's time budget; her entry is marked minimal. Two write-in candidates (Gage Thunder, no party preference; Dev Gupta, independent) are on the general-election ballot per Ballotpedia but have negligible public footprint and are not given full entries. Federal key votes and FEC totals are not applicable since neither major candidate is a sitting member of Congress; campaign finance totals mentioned in context come from Ballotpedia's own reporting, not verified FEC filings. Biographical detail for Monica Alponte comes only from her own Ballotpedia survey; no education, birthplace, or employer details were found.
